question.text: The tenor of a Cat II AIF scheme may be extended beyond the original close-ended period with:

answer.text: Consent of at least 2/3rd of unit-holders by value (per Regulation 13).
No approval needed - the manager has absolute discretion.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SEBI (AIF) Regulation 13 permits the fund tenor to be extended by up to 2 years with consent of at least 2/3rd of unit-holders by value of their investment. SEBI nod is not required for the extension itself but is implicit in the PPM framework. **The Trap:** SEBI-only centralises wrongly. Trustee-only gives trustee sole power. Manager-discretion is false - LP consent is mandatory. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A tests the 2/3rd rule at distributor level. XIX-C confirms. Ch 14 Regulatory covers Regulation 13. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Plan extensions 6 months before end-of-tenor; rushing an extension vote without early LP dialogue often triggers redemption-like pressure that blows up illiquid positions.
